title: Free $1,000 for Babies? Trump Accounts Are Here, But Some Families Are Still Waiting
summary:
Imagine getting a free $1,000 just for being born! That's the idea behind Trump Accounts, a new government program that gives seed money to babies born while Donald Trump is president. The president visited a high school in Georgia on Wednesday to talk about the accounts, which launched on July 4. But here's the catch: not every family has gotten their money yet.

The accounts work like a special savings jar. For every baby born from 2025 to 2028, the U.S. Treasury puts in $1,000 to start. Parents, relatives, and even friends can add more money over time. The cash gets invested in the stock market, which means it can grow bigger. But kids can't touch the money until they turn 18, and only for certain things like college, starting a business, or buying a home.

So far, 6.5 million kids have signed up, and 1.5 million of them are babies who qualify for the $1,000. That's a lot of piggy banks! But some parents are frustrated. Masaki and Kristina McLellan from New Jersey signed up their baby Maya in early July. At first, their application was rejected. After an hour on the phone, it was approved—but they were told the money could take up to four weeks to arrive. "We definitely want to give her options for her future," Kristina said. The government says most families get the money in just one or two days, but they give longer estimates just in case.

Not everyone thinks the program is perfect. Some people say it doesn't help families right now, when little kids might need food or a safe place to live. Others point out that the same big bill that created Trump Accounts also cut money from programs like Medicaid, which helps kids see doctors. Still, supporters say it gives all kids a fair shot at building wealth, not just rich ones.
why_it_matters: This shows that even a free-money program can have delays and disagreements, and it reminds you to think about saving for big future goals like college.

keywords.explanation: Seed money is a starting amount of money that helps something grow, like planting a seed.
The stock market is a place where people buy and sell tiny pieces of companies, hoping their value will go up.
The U.S. Treasury is the government department that prints money, collects taxes, and pays the nation’s bills.
When money is invested, it is put into something like the stock market so it can grow over time.
Medicaid is a U.S. government program that helps people with low incomes pay for doctor visits and medicine.
Wealth means having a lot of money and valuable things like a house, a business, or savings.

background_read: For many years, some people wanted to give every child a savings account at birth to help them later in life, an idea once called 'baby bonds'.
The U.S. Treasury (the government’s money department) runs these Trump Accounts and makes the $1,000 deposits.
The same big law that created these accounts also made changes to Medicaid, a program that helps poor families see doctors, which worried some people.

WHERE: Across the United States, with an announcement at a high school in Georgia.
WHY: To help kids build wealth for college, a business, or a home, while also sparking debate about other cuts.
